items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: So he put me with the Basie Band in 1950... I’ll tell you working with Count Basie was like, we were a family... Bill Basie was one of the nicest people in the whole world.

ctx.x: Yeah. He cared enough to get angry I guess.
Yeah. He cared enough to get angry. And so that was a great experience. Then I heard Benny Goodman. Oh I heard Johnny Mince first. He played with Tommy Dorsey’s band. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

And my brother and I would go to the Earle Theater in Philadelphia and sit there all day on a Saturday, five, six shows, and see every show. And I watched Johnny Mince play with Tommy Dorsey and I thought I’d really like to do that, play jazz. And then of course Benny Goodman, and then Benny Goodman was, I would say responsible for putting the jazz clarinet on the map. Then Artie Shaw. And Artie Shaw to me was, he might still be my favorite today. So one thing led to another and I wanted to play jazz. I told my…

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And there I learned economy in playing from Bill Basie.

ctx.x: Right. What was the reaction of audiences to that news?

It was a pretty good reaction, yeah, and there again, most of the audiences knew what they came to hear so they accepted what Bill Basie had to offer. And he was smart enough to make that small group sound almost like a big band and to never neglect the intent of the music and the rhythm and the feeling of the music. He never got carried away with so much stuff that you couldn’t, and which there again, was my problem when I had my big band, was too much. But Bill Basie, there I learned economy in playing from…
So many people talk about what he didn’t play.

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Oh yeah, Gene Krupa, Tommy Dorsey, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, all the big bands... they all came through and we’d devour that music.

ctx.x: Do you remember any in particular? You mentioned Tommy Dorsey when you heard Johnny Mintz.
Oh yeah, Gene Krupa, Tommy Dorsey, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, all the big bands, Benny Goodman, Artie Shaw…
Amazing. DeFranco:…they all came through and we’d devour that music. Most of the BandBusters were there watching those shows.
